newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Govt offered Murdoch deal on Seven - paper.
newsitem.headline: Govt offered Murdoch deal on Seven - paper.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard offered to allow Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd a higher stake in Seven Network Ltd if Murdoch would support a takeover by Kerry Packer of John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, The Australian Financial Review reported on Friday.
But the plan fell apart last week when News rejected another element of the deal which would have required News sell some of its Australian newspapers, the newspaper said.

"It is understood that in a meeting early last week with News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley, and with Rupert Murdoch participating via telephone, Howard said the government would ease the foreign investment rules for television if News agreed to support the government's plan to abolish cross-media ownership rules," the Financial Review.
News has a 14 percent stake in Seven Network and rules governing foreign investment in the media stop News from raising that stake beyond 15 percent.
The cross-media rules set up by the former Labor government prevent television station owners from owning a major newspaper in the same city or vice versa.
These rules stop Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd increasing its Fairfax stake beyond 15 percent while it owns the top-rating Nine television network.
The conservative Liberal/National government, which has criticised the cross-media rules as outdated, is widely expected to scrap the rules soon, allowing Packer to launch a bid for Fairfax.
PBL currently owns about 12 percent of Fairfax.

"By urging News Ltd to divest, thereby allowing a new publisher into the newspaper market, the government hoped to mute mounting criticism about lack of ownership diversity should Packer take over Fairfax," the Financial Review said.
Fairfax's shares closed up 10 cents at A$3.27 on Thursday as speculation of a takeover bid was rekindled.
